content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Release Date: August 13, 2026
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
Positive Points
-
Newsmax Inc (NYSE:NMAX) achieved its first profitable quarter as a public company, with net income of $2.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.7 million.
-
Total revenue reached a record $54.1 million, up 16.5% year-over-year, driven by a 20.5% increase in broadcast revenue.
-
Affiliate fee revenue surged 81.9% year-over-year to $13.4 million, reflecting new contracts and rate increases, with significant room to close the gap with peers.
-
International licensing is expanding rapidly, with 2026 fees expected to reach $16 million (a 344% increase) and a new launch in Poland, supported by multi-year agreements.
-
The company secured a multi-year AI content partnership with Meta, positioning Newsmax at the forefront of AI-driven news distribution and opening a new potential revenue stream.
-
Gross margin expanded to 43.1% from 38% in the prior year, driven by higher-margin affiliate and licensing revenue and improved operating efficiencies.
-
The balance sheet remains strong with $128.3 million in cash and investments and no debt, providing financial flexibility for growth investments.
-
Total viewership reached 26.9 million, up 4% year-over-year, marking the highest second-quarter reach in four years, with strong engagement among adults 35-64.
-
Social media followers grew over 28% year-over-year to over 26 million, enhancing brand reach and cross-promotion opportunities.
-
The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $212-$216 million, representing 13% growth at the midpoint, with expectations for improved operating profile.
Negative Points
-
Advertising revenue declined 3.5% year-over-year to $28.8 million, due to lower customer order volume and challenging comparisons from election-related demand.
-
Digital revenue decreased 1.3% year-over-year to $8.3 million, as growth in digital advertising was offset by lower subscription revenue and product sales.
-
Subscription revenue fell 9.9% year-over-year to $6.3 million, driven by lower new customer acquisition.
-
Product sales revenue dropped 31.7% year-over-year to $1.1 million, primarily due to decreased book and supplement sales.
-
The company remains in strategic investment mode, which could pressure near-term margins despite profitability, as it continues to invest in programming, technology, and OTT initiatives.
-
The AI partnership with Meta is in early stages, and its contribution to revenue is not yet quantified, with no guidance provided for future AI-related income.
-
Affiliate fee rates remain approximately 7 times below peers, and the pace of closing this gap is uncertain and dependent on continued execution.
-
The company faces a challenging advertising environment, with a decline in ad revenue despite overall growth, indicating potential volatility in this segment.
-
International licensing, while growing, is still a relatively small portion of total revenue, and future growth beyond 2027 is not guaranteed.
-
The company's profitability was aided by the absence of prior-year legal settlement expenses, which may not recur, potentially affecting year-over-year comparisons.
Q & A Highlights
Q: What percentage of your subscriber base is scheduled for renewal over the next 12 to 24 months, and how quickly can you close the affiliate rate gap with peers without sacrificing distribution? A: CFO Daryl Burnham stated the company does not publicly disclose the percentage of affiliate fees up for renewal but highlighted that the strategy is already showing results, with affiliate revenues up 81.9% year-over-year in Q2 2026. CEO Chris Ruddy added that the best leverage is ratings and growing brand value, noting the company has successfully secured renewals from every major player. Closing the seven-times rate gap depends on continued execution of the strategic vision in programming, talent, and distribution.
Q: How much of the $16 million international licensing guidance is already contracted, and how should we think about licensing growth into 2027? A: CFO Daryl Burnham confirmed the $16 million guidance for 2026 is based on factual agreements already in place and is not contingent on future deals. The company has previously indicated a $25 million annualized run rate for 2027, reflecting strong global interest in conservative news. CEO Chris Ruddy added that all agreements are multi-year, with renewals already secured on the main deal in Serbia, and sees international licensing as a huge area of opportunity.
Q: Can you discuss the economics of the Meta AI content partnership and are you in discussions with other major AI platforms? A: CEO Chris Ruddy declined to reveal financial details but described it as a multi-year agreement consistent with market rates and "very powerful." He emphasized that Meta, which is investing over $100 billion in AI, sees Newsmax as an important partner. The company is in discussions with a number of AI companies and views this as the beginning of its AI efforts, potentially becoming a significant licensing stream. CFO Daryl Burnham added that AI is becoming an important channel for news discovery, and the partnership validates the strength of the Newsmax brand.
Q: Can you dig into the margin improvements related to improved operating efficiencies outside of higher affiliate fees? A: CFO Daryl Burnham attributed the gross margin expansion to 43.1% from 38% to high-margin affiliate fee and licensing revenue growth, as well as operating efficiencies gained after the first year as a public company. He noted the absence of first-year public company expenses and legal costs, and highlighted the use of new tools, including AI, to become more efficient in content generation and production. CEO Chris Ruddy added that AI speeds up the process of putting content together, reduces costs in digital, TV production, and graphics, though all content still requires human verification.
Q: Is the content investment margin expansion due to lower content costs from AI implementation, or other avenues? A: CFO Daryl Burnham explained that investments in programming and content drive ratings, which increase advertiser demand and create economies of scale. These investments also enhance the value proposition for Newsmax Plus streaming and strengthen the company's negotiating position for affiliate fees. CEO Chris Ruddy clarified that the company is not yet implementing an AI feature on Newsmax itself, but is partnering with companies like Meta to provide content for AI models.
Q: To what extent is social media a funnel to Newsmax 2 and Newsmax Plus, and how do you view the user acquisition funnel? A: CEO Chris Ruddy rejected the "funnel" concept, preferring "cross-promoting" across all platforms. He explained that TV promotes digital and vice versa, with the app and notifications driving traffic across all channels. This synergistic approach has made Newsmax one of the top 12 U.S. news brands according to Reuters, and the company expects revenue monetization to grow significantly due to its brand and reach.
Q: What could the midterms mean for audience engagement, sales, and profits for the back half of 2026? A: CEO Chris Ruddy noted that elections are always good for engagement, though midterm advertising is often local-oriented. He expects increased engagement after the midterms due to the likelihood of a divided government, which tends to generate more news and conflicting stories. Additionally, the presidential campaign will begin in earnest, with at least a half dozen candidates expected, creating a "two-year great window" for continued growth and reach across all platforms.
Q: Can the AI licensing become a meaningful standalone revenue stream going forward? A: CEO Chris Ruddy confirmed it is already a standalone revenue stream and expressed hope it could become a significant licensing stream, noting that AI companies need content and Newsmax has a lot of it. CFO Daryl Burnham added that while no specific guidance is provided, the company is excited to participate in the AI growth story and hopes it becomes meaningful over time.
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
